questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which lanthanoid readily shows the +4 oxidation state in aqueous solution and acts as a strong oxidising agent?
questions.explanation: Cerium loses its 4f and 5d electrons to form Ce⁴⁺, which has the xenon noble-gas configuration, so Ce⁴⁺ is a strong oxidising agent. Eu and Yb prefer +2, and Lu is found only in +3.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Lanthanoids: oxidation states
questions.reason: Explanation is factually wrong: it says Ce loses its 4f and 5d electrons to form Ce4+, but Ce4+ ([Xe]) requires losing four electrons (4f1, 5d1 and both 6s2). Key B itself is correct; the explanation needs rewriting before reuse.
